intervals.label: collaboration
intervals.note: Bounds are those of the detector run; no source gives the collaboration's own formation or dissolution date.
intervals.quote: IMB was an 8,000 ton Cherenkov detector — a device able to spot a form of electromagnetic radiation that is used for particle identification — that operated between 1982 and 1991.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.note: Year precision; the collaboration's formal end is not published.
intervals.quote: IMB’s run ended in 1991, but its impact continues today.

name: IMB Collaboration
notes: Formation date and membership counts are not published in the sources consulted; the sixteen institutions are those on the author list of the 1987 paper and are not recorded as membership rows.

summary.plain: The group of about a dozen universities and laboratories, led by Irvine, Michigan and Brookhaven, that built and ran the IMB water detector in an Ohio salt mine from 1982 to 1991.
summary.technical: IMB (Irvine-Michigan-Brookhaven) collaboration: Irvine, Michigan, BNL, Caltech/JPL, Cleveland State, Hawaii, UCL, Warsaw, Case Western, Illinois, Berkeley, LLNL, Notre Dame, Boston, Fermilab and AT&T Bell Laboratories on the 1987 SN 1987A paper.
